tagline: Fifteen interstate miles over the world's longest bayou.
intro: An unlikely byway, and a plain four-lane freeway. From Highway 256 at White Hall, I-530 swings around the southwest side of Pine Bluff for 15 miles, flat across the Mississippi Alluvial Plain, to US 65 southeast of town. Its exit numbers climb southward, backward at first glance, because a spur counts its miles from where it leaves the parent road, up at Little Rock.
Locally the bypass is the Wiley Branton Highway, named for the Pine Bluff civil rights lawyer who filed the suit against the Little Rock School Board.

moments.title: White Hall
moments.text: The byway begins in this small city north of Pine Bluff, home to the Pine Bluff Arsenal.

moments.title: Bayou Bartholomew
moments.text: The highway crosses the world's longest bayou, a slow stream in an old bed of the Arkansas River with more than a hundred kinds of fish, among bald cypress and wetland.
